On 2023-05-20, the user asked whether pulsar timing measurements had confirmed general relativity with respect to Sirius’s mass. The assistant clarified that pulsar timing was not used to confirm Sirius’s mass; it has tested other aspects of general relativity, while Sirius’s mass is determined through other astronomical methods.

Astronomers analyze stellar spectra by separating starlight into wavelengths and comparing absorption-line positions and intensities with known elemental spectra to identify elements in a star’s atmosphere. They estimate temperature from the spectrum’s shape: hotter stars emit relatively more energy at shorter wavelengths, while cooler stars emit relatively more at longer wavelengths.

Astronomers use stellar chemical compositions to study the history of star formation: stars from different generations can have different compositions, and their spectra provide evidence about conditions when they formed.

A star’s temperature and size are related to how long it burns fuel. Astronomers use spectra, luminosity, and other properties to estimate stellar ages and evolutionary stages, and compare lifetimes across stars of different masses.
Spectra of supernova explosions can reveal the composition of a massive star’s outer layers and conditions during the explosion, helping astronomers investigate how supernovae occur.

Metal-poor stars, which formed when the early universe contained mostly hydrogen and helium and few heavier elements, have spectra that provide clues about early-universe conditions and nucleosynthesis.
Extremely metal-rich stars likely formed from material ejected by earlier generations of stars; their spectra help researchers study the chemical evolution of galaxies.

Studying the compositions of stars that host exoplanets can provide information about the formation and evolution of planetary systems, including whether systems with giant gas planets like Jupiter are rare or common.
Variable stars change brightness over time. Their spectra can help investigate causes such as pulsations, stellar flares, and eclipsing binary systems.
